input:
Performance of a natural-draft cooling tower at a chemical site was logged over one summer month. The mean wet-bulb temperature of the air over the month was 23 °C. The tower's approach was 3 K and its range was 10 K. The approach is the difference between the temperature of the water leaving the tower and the wet-bulb temperature of the air entering it; it states how closely the tower brings the water to the limit the air condition sets. The range is the difference between the temperature of the water entering the tower and the temperature of the water leaving it; it states the cooling the tower achieved across the logged month.

The two figures describe different things and are not interchangeable. The range depends on the heat load placed on the tower as much as on the tower itself, while the approach depends on the tower and on the wet-bulb temperature it worked against. An approach of 3 K at a mean wet-bulb temperature of 23 °C is the tighter statement of the pair: it fixes the leaving-water condition the tower reached under the air conditions of that month, and it is the figure a comparison with another period has to be made on.

The record carries the limit of its period. Performance was logged over one summer month, and performance outside the logged month was not measured. In particular, performance at winter wet-bulb temperatures is absent from the record: the tower's behaviour under the lower wet-bulb temperatures of winter, when both the approach it can hold and the load placed on it differ from the summer values, is not established by this log and is not claimed here.
